claims.statement: `ImportCsvModal` contains no file input, sample picker, preview, result summary or `unconfigured` branch: it owns an Escape listener and a click-away scrim and renders a fixed EmptyState saying importing is unavailable, with the only prop `onClose`.

`ImportCsvModal` is reachable in the app shell not from `app/` but from `modules/shell/ui/Sidebar.tsx`, which maps the Operations item `{ label: 'Import records', op: 'import' }` onto `NavRow`'s `onOp` and renders the modal from `activeOp`; `resolveOperations` filters the row out on trainer routes, so only office users can open it.
`tests/unit/sidebar.test.ts` pins the modal's prop surface: the import overlay receives only `onClose` and raises no toast, unlike `SettingsModal` which does get props and an `onSaved` toast.

`importLearnersCsv` runs an ordered pipeline — `isSupabaseConfigured()` gate returning `unconfigured`, pure parse and validate, an RLS-scoped `select` of the batch's `tenant_id`, a read of existing `(id, uli)`, insert of unmatched rows with their details, then per-row updates — so the tenant of a write is never accepted as an argument but read back off a batch the caller could already read.

The import has no transaction and no rollback: `learners` and `learner_details` are separate requests, an insert failure skips the update step entirely, and `summariseWrites` grades `ok`, `sync-failed` (nothing saved) or `partial` (real counts plus the raw error). Re-importing the same file converges because rows match on ULI and details upsert.

The two write halves have intentionally different widths: `learners` receives a fixed literal of `learner_no`, the four name columns and `assessment_result`, while the 23 T2MIS cells go to `learner_details` as a `Partial` upserted on `learner_id`, with the query skipped entirely when no detail cell was filled — so a names-only re-import never blanks earlier details.

The T2MIS detail cells map into `learner_details` rather than `learners` because RLS filters rows and not columns: `learners` is readable by a trainer for their own batches, so dates of birth, contact numbers and salary would otherwise be reachable by any assigned trainer, while the import runs as an admin/coordinator who holds `can_manage_tenant`.

`validateRows` rejects a row in a fixed order — missing last/first name, `uli` outside `/^[A-Za-z0-9-]{8,20}$/`, any parse-stage problem, then a ULI already seen in the file — and a rejected row is skipped and reported rather than imported; only a file where nothing survives is `validation-failed`.

An unrecognised assessment result is a row error rather than a silent default to `pending` (importing `Competnt` as pending would understate the batch's results), while a blank cell legitimately means `pending`.
A ULI repeated within the uploaded file is rejected at validation so the database's partial unique index is never what fails; the second occurrence loses.

Only one batch per file is accepted: if either `training calendar code` or `qualification program title` carries more than one distinct value the file is refused outright as `multiple-batches` with the offending values named, because an import targets a single already-chosen batch and would otherwise file a whole-school sheet under one batch.

Reconciliation is application-side on ULI because no index supabase-js `onConflict` could target exists on it: `learners`' unique constraint is `(tenant_id, batch_id, learner_no)` and the ULI index added by `20261111120000` is partial (`where uli is not null`). Reconciliation is therefore scoped inside one batch, so the same ULI at another school inserts instead of colliding.

A `learner_details` row is an upsert with `onConflict: 'learner_id'` on the table's primary key, one object per call, which is what makes a sparser re-import update only the columns it carries; a learner id that cannot be recovered from the insert's `.select('id, uli')` is reported as a saved learner whose details could not be linked.

Coded T2MIS values are plain `text` with no `CHECK` on purpose because TESDA's value lists are unconfirmed and a wrong list would reject rows T2MIS accepts; `sex` is the sole constrained column, which is why the parser normalises it through an alias map and flags anything else.

`domain/t2mis.ts` is the single ordered source of truth for the T2MIS sheet: 48 `{ header, value }` columns with TESDA's strings verbatim, including the trailing space in `'Province '` and the two columns both called `Municipality City`; `T2MIS_HEADERS` derives from it and is pinned at 48 in order.

The layout lives in `import-export/domain/` while the workbook writer lives in `modules/reports`, so the export reaches the layout as a legal cross-module `domain/` import rather than a blocked `data/`-to-`data/` one; `batches/data/learners.ts` imports `ageOn` from the same file the same way.

The export's own row builder and `parseLearnerCsv` are inverses: a test round-trips an exported 48-cell row through parse and validate, expecting zero errors and the same learner columns, so the import's shape is held to the export's.

The pipeline parses an Excel-serial date cell bound to serials 20000–80000 (1954..2119) and normalises `MM/DD/YYYY` and ISO to ISO, so a stray small integer such as an age is refused as a date instead of being read as one.

Because the T2MIS sheet repeats 'Municipality City' and 'Province' for provider and learner, `rowsToRecords` keys by header and the later — learner — cell wins, so the provider cells are dropped from this import; the wider provider/qualification columns are the export's concern only.

`importLearnersCsv` has never executed against a live database because no Supabase env exists in this environment; only the `domain/` layer plus the pure `summariseWrites` are unit-tested, and `importLearnersCsv` is typechecked only, so a policy, FK or constraint failure would first appear in production.

The import is an internal working copy that touches only `learners` and `learner_details`: it creates no batches, links no `tenant_qualifications`, writes no documents, evidence or `activity_log`, never deletes (ADR-001 T2), and has no adapter to map raw database error text to user copy — a `TODO` against rule 6.

The unimplemented wiring is a caller action, and the batch to import into is unresolved: the modal is opened from a global sidebar with no batch context, so the wiring must both take a file and choose a batch, then an `unconfigured` disable and a renderer for the discriminated result.

`domain/csv.ts` is a dependency-free RFC 4180 scanner kept in `domain/` rather than `data/` because domain layers are pure (rule 14), handling quoted fields, escaped `""`, `\r\n` and `\n` and an unterminated trailing cell.

A change to the import must keep new columns in `learner_details` and the `DETAIL_COLUMNS` map rather than the fixed `learners` literal, or a names-only re-import starts blanking data; a new column also needs a migration and `database.types.ts` regeneration first.

`importLearnersCsv` runs `validation-failed` checks before any network call (each parse status maps to a distinct error string), then enters a try/catch in which a failure to read the batch's tenant or the batch's existing `(id, uli)` rows returns `sync-failed` with the raw database text, and any thrown error is caught into a `sync-failed` carrying the thrown message.

An insert-step failure skips the update step entirely (`inserted.error ? { saved: 0, error: null } : await updateLearners(...)`), so a partial insert never also half-applies updates to already-matched rows.

`learners` rows are updated one at a time (supabase-js has no bulk update with per-row values), and `saved` only increments after that row's learner update *and* details write both succeed — which is why `partial` counts always mean fully-applied rows.
The importer's tests cover the parser, validator, reconciler and `summariseWrites`, but never execute `importLearnersCsv`, so a green suite says the domain layer is right, not that the import works.

Module README and every file header still call the shipped modal a TES-49 blocker saying importing is unavailable, but `ImportCsvModal` is today a complete intake screen: a required file input restricted to `.csv` that reads `File.text()`, a result-panel state machine, an `unconfigured` notice and a client-side config probe — only the batch selector is missing, and the shell passes `tenant` but no `batchId`.

`importLearnersCsv` is a Server Action driven from the client through `startTransition`, its result is kept in `result` state and rendered as a `role="status"` panel, and `unconfigured` is handled by leaving the form mounted with the button disabled — so the browser really reaches the `data/` layer even though nothing in `app/` composes the modal.

Because there is still no batch picker, the modal does not call `importLearnersCsv` until the caller starts passing a `batchId`; the action stores whatever id it was handed in `batchId`, so the picker is the one missing wiring seam.

The result renderer gives every status a distinct panel: each `validation-failed` error is listed, `skipped` rows render as `Row N (ULI) — reason`, `partial` carries an explicit saved-vs-not statement plus the raw error, `sync-failed`/`unconfigured` say nothing was saved, and any result is fronted with 'not a TESDA submission' (rule 27) — so the raw driver text reaches the panel and the rule 6 mapping TODO is still open.

`validateRows` reports rejects rather than dropping them, and a matched ULI is updated rather than skipped: a surviving row becomes `toUpdate`, a rejected row becomes `skipped` whenever at least one row survives, and a blank assessment cell combined with an unmatched ULI is the only way to create a `pending` row — so a blank cell alone never clears an existing result.

`parseT2misDate` is the single date reader for both directions and its laxness is load-bearing: a bare MM/DD/YYYY, a one-digit month or day and a five-digit Excel serial in 20000–80000 all yield a date and never an error, so `31/12/1990` imports as 31 December while the row is refused only for its unrecognised sex — and since `DD/MM/YYYY` passes the regex by accident it can silently swap month and day (02/04/1961 reads as 4 February).

The ULI rule is stricter than the schema: `validateRows` rejects any ULI outside `/^[A-Za-z0-9-]{8,20}$/` (a soft shape check, not TESDA's algorithm) while `learners.uli` is nullable and the export writes a blank cell for a missing one, so a null-ULI learner can never be updated by a re-import and comes back as a new insert.

A ULI-keyed import can write onto the wrong grader's batch id in a flat course: the export falls back to the batch's `start_date`/`end_date` and program name for cells the scholar has no value for, and `parseLearnerCsv` never reads those back, so the batch-level dates are lost and the poster decides.

`learners_tenant_batch_uli_key` is unique only where `uli is not null`, so any number of null-ULI learners coexist in a batch (the reason the import's ULI column is optional and the export writes a blank cell) and the applied table holds no `(tenant_id, batch_id, learner_no)` constraint at all — the reconciler's “learner_no is only unique per batch” comment is stale.

Import and export are one file format read in two directions, held together by design: the 48-cell export row is fed back through `parseLearnerCsv` and `validateRows` in a test and must produce no errors and the same learner columns, and the escape hatch is that the parser's header aliases accept both the export's 'Assessment Results' and a roster CSV.

Adding a column means a migration first, then `database.types.ts`, then the parser map: switching the `DETAIL_COLUMNS` map is how a T2MIS column reaches `learner_details`, and coded values stay plain `text` so T2MIS's own value lists are never overruled by a `CHECK`.
